assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy turned a gut-hormone discovery into drugs that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with effects on weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The path from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to long-acting agonists is clear, original and of very large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (biology, intestinotropic and cardiometabolic actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form and its insulinotropic action) form a plausible three-person set. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen led the pharmaceutical development of liraglutide and semaglutide and is a strong alternative; other early contributors not on the list (for example Habener) cannot be proposed. The three-person cap forces a difficult choice between discovery biology and drug development.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is established in large independent trials and real-world use over more than a decade; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between peptide identification, physiology and drug development is contested.
Knudsen is excluded from my proposed set only because of the three-name limit; this is a judgement call.
Long-term safety data for the newest agents are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method to control defined cell populations with light, which changed circuit analysis across the nervous system and beyond; the tool is among the most widely adopted of the past two decades. The discovery is original, clear and of lasting methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment as a neuronal control tool in mammalian neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive; Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation is also a distinct claim. Six credited names for a three-person prize is the main difficulty. My set pairs the molecular discovery with the neuroscience implementation.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is overwhelming and the method is mature; recognition is timely. Clinical translation is only beginning (retinal optogenetics) and is not needed for the case.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six credited people is unresolved and the choice of three excludes Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck.
It is a tool rather than a disease mechanism, which some may weigh against a physiology or medicine award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs, with expanding use in other cancers and autoimmune disease. Clinical impact is dramatic and the concept is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulation, first durable responses) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and CAR design, preclinical proof) are central. Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and TIL work are important antecedents and early CAR clinical trials; Zelig Eshhar, the originator of the chimeric receptor concept, is not on the credited list, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; solid tumours remain largely unresolved, and safety (cytokine release, neurotoxicity, secondary malignancy signals) is still monitored.
uncertainties: The omission of the original chimeric-receptor concept originator from the credited list limits attribution.
Whether Rosenberg should replace one of the proposed laureates is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing, culminating in nusinersen, converted spinal muscular atrophy from a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one, and established splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic modality. The mechanistic insight and clinical effect are both strong.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory elements and the ISS-N1 antisense strategy with Bennett developing the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug at Ionis; the two-person credit is coherent. Other contributors to SMN2 biology and trial work exist but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with years of clinical follow-up and independent confirmation; the modality has since spread. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Contribution of the SMN gene discovery and other antisense groups is outside the supplied credit.
Long-term outcomes and relative merit versus gene therapy continue to be evaluated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR is a central controller of growth and metabolism linking nutrient signals to protein synthesis, with consequences in cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and metabolic disease. The discovery of TOR through rapamycin resistance in yeast and its conservation in mammals is original and has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genes and their function in growth control and is the most clearly decisive contributor. Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and the identification of the mammalian target is a distinct, defensible second contribution; Sabatini contributed to mTOR biochemistry (mTORC1/2 regulation) but is not in my proposed set because the core discovery precedes his work.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed by many independent groups and has produced approved drugs (rapalogs); the field is mature, and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should include biochemical dissection of mTORC1 and mTORC2 is uncertain.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) reframed how cells compartmentalize biochemistry and has affected cell biology, neurodegeneration and gene regulation research broadly.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule work from Brangwynne and Hyman is the founding demonstration; Görlich and McKnight contributed related work on low-complexity domains and FG-repeat hydrogels. A two-person pair is cleanest, but four credited names reflect real disagreement on priority.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely adopted, but the physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms in vivo is still debated and quantitative standards are evolving. Recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Debate about which condensates truly form by phase separation in cells.
Credit among four people is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL kinase inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable chronic condition and proved the principle of targeted cancer therapy, and Sawyers' work on resistance mutations guided second-generation inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and trials), Lydon (discovery programme at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis) and Sawyers (resistance mechanism and next-generation therapy) are well matched to the clinical arc. The earlier discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion and the chemistry of the compound (Zimmermann) are antecedents not in the credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than twenty years of survival data and independent confirmation. Recognition is arguably late; the main issue is that prior prizes recognized adjacent areas.
uncertainties: Scientific credit for the compound chemistry is outside the supplied names.
Some may regard the contribution as translational rather than a fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A was identified as the repressor of fetal hemoglobin through human genetics and mechanistic work, which led to the first approved CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, an elegant genetic-to-therapy path.
assessment.attribution: Orkin established the BCL11A mechanism, Sankaran identified it through GWAS-guided biology, and Bauer developed the enhancer-editing strategy. Swee Lay Thein's genetic association work on HbF levels is also important and excluded only by the cap.
assessment.maturity: Therapy is approved but follow-up is limited to a few years and access is constrained; the genetic mechanism is well confirmed. Slightly early for the clinical component.
uncertainties: Whether the gene-editing therapy belongs in the same prize as other CRISPR-related recognition.
Credit among four people is unresolved, including the role of Thein.
